Package gov.cdc.izgateway.db

Class RefreshQueueService

java.lang.Object
gov.cdc.izgateway.db.RefreshQueueService
@Service public class RefreshQueueService extends Object
A service to send refresh messages to other instances via SQS and await their responses.

  • Constructor Details

    • RefreshQueueService

      @Autowired public RefreshQueueService(DbController.DbControllerConfiguration configuration, gov.cdc.izgateway.service.impl.EndpointStatusService endpointStatusService, ApiKeyPrincipalProvider apiKeyPrincipalProvider, gov.cdc.izgateway.repository.IHostRepository hostService)
      Create the messaging service.

      This bean depends on services only. It must never depend on a controller: a controller on the dependency path of the listener thread is what forced the earlier new RefreshQueueService(...) and kept StatusController from reaching it. See IGDD-3599.

      Parameters:
      configuration - Reloads cached configuration from the datastore
      endpointStatusService - Clears circuit breakers
      apiKeyPrincipalProvider - Evicts a cached API key credential
      hostService - Lists the known instances and their regions

  • Method Details

    • myHostName

      public static String myHostName()
      Get the host name of this instance.

      org.apache.commons.lang3.SystemUtils.getHostName() reads the HOSTNAME environment variable and returns null when it is not set. A null here builds the queue name izgw_null_refresh-requests. The fallback keeps the primary value whenever HOSTNAME is set, which it always is in the deployed container. See IGDD-3599.

      Returns:
      The host name, never null

    • distribute

      public Map<String,String> distribute(RefreshQueueService.RefreshRequest request, Map<String,String> results)
      Send a command to every known instance other than the caller, then wait for the replies.

      The caller identifies itself through senderHost and senderRegion on the request. Those values decide which entry is skipped, so a caller keeps its own notion of the local host name rather than inheriting one from this class.

      Parameters:
      request - The command to send. Its sender fields identify the caller
      results - The outcome map to fill in, keyed region:hostname
      Returns:
      the same map, with one entry per instance reached

    • summarizeByRegion

      public static Map<String,String> summarizeByRegion(Map<String,String> results)
      Reduce per-instance outcomes to one status per region.

      The result carries no host name and no instance count, so a consumer can forward it to an untrusted client without redacting it. See IGDD-3599, design decision D5.

      Parameters:
      results - Outcomes keyed region:hostname
      Returns:
      one of complete, partial or failed per region

    • applyLocally

      public String applyLocally(RefreshQueueService.RefreshRequest request)
      Apply a command on this instance, in process.

      CAUTION: this method must never call a REST endpoint of this instance. If it did, and that endpoint distributes commands, every receiving instance would distribute again and the operation would never terminate. See IGDD-3599, design decision D4.

      Authorization is not rechecked here. The operator's request was authorized once, on the instance that received it, and this message arrived on a queue that only Hub instances can write to.

      Public because both controllers apply commands through it. The reset endpoints must call it for the instance that serves the request: distribute(gov.cdc.izgateway.db.RefreshQueueService.RefreshRequest, java.util.Map<java.lang.String, java.lang.String>) skips the caller, so without this the serving instance is the one instance that never resets.

      Parameters:
      request - The command to apply
      Returns:
      "OK" when every requested action succeeded, otherwise a short description of the failure
